stem: Copper is a transition element and has atomic number 29.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete the electronic configuration for the copper atom and the copper ion in the +2 oxidation state.

- copper atom [Ar]

- copper ion in the +2 oxidation state [Ar]

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The following equilibrium exists between two complex ions of copper in the +2 oxidation state.

$$\text{[Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} + 4\text{Cl}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{[CuCl}_4]^{2-} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction occurring here.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the colours of these two complex ions.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State the shape of the $\text{[CuCl}_4]^{2-}$ ion.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Write the expression for the stability constant, $K_{\text{stab}}$, for this equilibrium.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Copper also forms the complex ions $\text{[Cu(NH}_3)_2\text{(H}_2\text{O)}_4]^{2+}$ and $\text{[Cu}(en)\text{(H}_2\text{O)}_4]^{2+}$ where $en$ is the bidentate ligand ethane-1,2-diamine, $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$.

$$\text{[Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} + 2\text{NH}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{[Cu(NH}_3)_2\text{(H}_2\text{O)}_4]^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$ equilibrium 1

$$\text{[Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} + en \rightleftharpoons \text{[Cu}(en)\text{(H}_2\text{O)}_4]^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$ equilibrium 2

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: What is meant by the term bidentate ligand?

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The table lists the values of stability constants for these two complexes.

|  | stability constant, $K_{\text{stab}}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{[Cu(NH}_3)_2\text{(H}_2\text{O)}_4]^{2+}$ | $7.94 \times 10^{7}$ |
| $\text{[Cu}(en)\text{(H}_2\text{O)}_4]^{2+}$ | $3.98 \times 10^{10}$ |

What do these $K_{\text{stab}}$ values tell us about the relative positions of equilibria 1 and 2?

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Nickel forms the complex ion $\text{[Ni}(en)_3]^{2+}$ in which it is surrounded octahedrally by six nitrogen atoms.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Name the type of stereoisomerism displayed by $\text{[Ni}(en)_3]^{2+}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Draw three-dimensional diagrams to show the two stereoisomers of $\text{[Ni}(en)_3]^{2+}$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Ethane-1,2-diamine is a useful reagent in organic chemistry.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Explain how the amino groups in ethane-1,2-diamine allow the molecule to act as a Brønsted-Lowry base.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of ethane-1,2-diamine with an excess of hydrochloric acid.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.text:
Under certain conditions, ethane-1,2-diamine reacts with ethanedioic acid, $\text{HO}_2\text{CCO}_2\text{H}$, to form the polymer $\mathbf{Z}$.

Draw the structure of this polymer, $\mathbf{Z}$, showing two repeat units.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction occurring during this polymerisation.

parts.label: (f)(iii)
parts.text:
Polymer $\mathbf{Z}$ is an example of a biodegradable polymer.

Name a polymer that is non-biodegradable.
